cycle.problem: SMTP acceptance before DB commit can deliver an unusable OTP; ambiguous acceptance plus rollback permits duplicate immediate emails
cycle.hypothesis: Commit OTP and cooldown before SMTP
cycle.revalidation: Commit failure sends zero messages; ambiguous acceptance preserves consumable code, immediate retry 429; real loopback greeting timeout ~15s then recovery 202 after cooldown

cycle.problem: Deleting an old photo after commit raises to the client and leaves an orphan; file writes before rollback can also remain
cycle.hypothesis: Persist candidates before writing/committing, then recheck committed references under Cat lock
cycle.revalidation: Upload returns 204 during cleanup failure; a new cleanup worker recovers it; rollback preserves active file and removes uncommitted file; nowait lock defers concurrent cleanup; references/legacy separators preserved

limitations: Disposable PostgreSQL, files and Mailpit only. FCM uses real sender/persisted receipts with isolated HTTP transport: partial and total 503 recovery; no Google delivery or physical phone.

SMTP timeout is per socket operation, not an end-to-end deadline. Commit-before-send does not provide a durable mail outbox, exactly-once SMTP, or delivery after process exit between commit/send; a failed send retains the 60s cooldown.
DB pause covers 0.5s stall/recovery and actual ~10s client ReadTimeout followed by recovery. It does not certify an API-side SQL deadline or crash/power-loss durability.

Cleanup journal targets the local private filesystem, with atomic candidate writes, up to 25 per sweep and 30s background interval. Failed candidates persist. This does not certify object stores, power loss or recovery of anonymous legacy temporary upload files.
Functional checks and bounded durations are not latency gains or capacity measurements.
